problem_type: timeout signal misclassified as user cancellation
symptom: A custom-call script interrupted by its own deadline could report that the user cancelled it, and the Linux unit lane intermittently observed the wrong classification.
direct_cause: The timeout controller aborted with an ordinary Error while classifyFailure inferred timeout only from Date.now() >= deadlineAt. A timer callback can run at the deadline boundary before the next clock read crosses it, so the already-aborted signal fell through to the generic cancelled branch.
class_root: Cancellation provenance was inferred from a second wall-clock read instead of being carried by the abort reason that caused the interruption.
affected_population: Users whose custom provider script reaches its execution deadline
Callers that propagate a standard TimeoutError abort reason into the custom-call runner
Linux CI workers whose timer and wall-clock reads expose the deadline-boundary race
internal_only_reason: Nomi owns the custom-call timeout and cancellation semantics. The standard TimeoutError name supplies provenance, but no external API determines the user-facing classification or runner contract.
invariants: The runner-created deadline abort carries the standard TimeoutError name.
A TimeoutError signal is classified as timeout even before a subsequent Date.now read crosses deadlineAt.
An ordinary external abort remains classified as cancellation.
The deadlineAt check remains a fail-safe for CPU-bound QuickJS interruption where the timer callback has not executed.
generality_proof: Both timeout sources converge on classifyFailure: runner-owned timers now carry explicit provenance, propagated TimeoutError signals retain that provenance, and the existing deadlineAt comparison still covers interrupt-handler deadlines. Generic abort reasons continue through the cancellation branch.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Attach explicit timeout provenance to runner-owned deadline aborts.
Map timeout, cancellation, and runtime failures from one authoritative signal/deadline boundary.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The timer aborts with an Error named TimeoutError instead of an untyped Error.
The relay preserves signal.reason, so upstream TimeoutError provenance reaches the classifier unchanged.
Every sandbox failure path already converges on classifyFailure, which now checks timeout provenance before generic cancellation.

recurrence.reason: Any deadline implemented as a generic abort can race a later wall-clock classification and be mislabeled as user cancellation.
same_class_scan: Searched the custom-call runner and sandbox for every AbortController, deadlineAt, signal.reason, timeout, and cancelled branch.
Verified the runner-owned timer and external signal relay both reach the same controller.
Checked the QuickJS interrupt loop and host sleep bridge for alternate classification paths.

prevention.invariant: Timeout provenance travels on AbortSignal.reason and is classified before generic cancellation or wall-clock fallback.
prevention.failure_mode: An untyped abort remains cancellation; a standard TimeoutError or elapsed deadline becomes timeout; runtime failures remain runtime errors.
prevention.strategy: Use a standard timeout reason at the producer, preserve it through signal relay, and assert classification without depending on timer scheduling.

legacy_paths.rationale: The supported runner and sandbox are corrected at their shared classification boundary; no parallel legacy timeout path exists.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The race is in Nomi-owned AbortSignal provenance and classification, not in QuickJS or Vitest versions.

migration: No state or protocol migration is required. Existing callers keep the same AbortSignal interface, and ordinary cancellation behavior is unchanged.
residual_risks: A third-party caller can label an unrelated abort reason TimeoutError; Nomi intentionally follows the standard reason identity supplied by the caller.
Wall-clock fallback remains necessary for CPU-bound interruption before the timeout callback runs.
